stories.title: Search Continues Near Otis for Two People Missing Since Wednesday
stories.summary: Search and rescue teams are looking for two local people missing near Otis since Wednesday morning, and the family is asking anyone in the area to keep an eye out. Misty Rose Aalto, 57, is 5'7", 180 lbs, with silver/blonde hair. Cyrus Buchholtz is 5'10", 185 lbs, with light brown/grey hair. The two are friends and local to the area. If you have seen them, or have any information at all, call 971-261-3027 or the Tillamook County Sheriff's Department. Misty and Cyrus were doing landscaping work at an Airbnb property on Savage Road in Otis, near the Salmon River, up Three Rock Road between Lincoln City and Neskowin. They were last seen Wednesday morning, November 25. Misty's daughter Patricia reported them missing around 5 p.m. Wednesday, after Airbnb guests arrived and found Misty's truck, purse, and dog still at the property, and a canoe missing. The family's flyer describes them as lost canoeing Wednesday morning, but it is not confirmed that they entered the water. The Tillamook County Sheriff's Office Search and Rescue team is actively searching. The U.S. Coast Guard assisted with a helicopter search of the mouth of the Salmon River and the shoreline and found no one. The search continued through the night into Thanksgiving, and a community search party was out on Thanksgiving Day. Conditions on the river this week have been hard: king tides, wind, and rain, with high water on the Salmon River. Anyone who was near the Salmon River, Three Rock Road, or Savage Road on Wednesday, or who has cameras in that area, is asked to check them and call with anything that might help: 971-261-3027 or the Tillamook County Sheriff's Department.
stories.img_credit: Photo of the Salmon River estuary from Cascade Head, the area being searched near Otis, by Lonelystudentwithtoomuchtime via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (licensed photo, Tillamook County Live original, 2026-11-26).

stories.title: A King Tide Wave Nearly Took a Man and His Dog at Cannon Beach
stories.summary: Just up the coast from Tillamook County, Tuesday morning's king tide gave the whole coast a lesson. Around 10:30 a.m. in Cannon Beach, a man standing on the beach-access stairs with his dog on a leash was hit by a surge that knocked both of them off their feet and dragged them along the seawall in the surf. Bystander video released by the Cannon Beach Police Department shows him clinging to the stair railing as wave after wave rolled over him. Both the man and the dog reached another set of stairs and got out of the water without injury. Police said the man had already been cited earlier in the day for driving on the beach, and people nearby said he had been warned about the surf more than once. Cannon Beach police released the video as a warning, and their list is worth taping to the fridge: beach-access stairs are not a safe place to watch king tides, never turn your back on the ocean, keep pets back from the surf, and stay off the driftwood, because big logs move in this water. The same conditions are running on Tillamook County beaches: king tides continue through Friday, a Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect, and a High Wind Watch runs into Wednesday morning as the next storm comes in. Watch the surf from high ground, stay off the rocks and jetties, and give the ocean room.
stories.img_credit: Photo of king tide surf breaking over the rocks at Rocky Creek State Scenic Viewpoint on the Oregon coast by Bonnie Moreland via Wikimedia Commons, public domain (licensed photo, Tillamook County Live original, 2026-11-24).

stories.title: Before the Flood Warning Even Starts, Rockaway Beach Has a Sandbag Crew
stories.summary: The worst of this week's water hasn't arrived yet. A Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect along the Tillamook County coast now, and a Coastal Flood Warning takes over Tuesday morning and runs through 4 a.m. Friday, with major flooding expected at high tides. Rockaway Beach didn't wait for it. Early Monday morning, Jason Hedler posted in the Rockaway Beach Community group with a simple offer: he will come fill and place sandbags for homes taking on water — free help, no charge. Less than an hour later, Terry Bryant of B Projects and Services LLC posted that he is bringing sandbags in from inland and will help get them set up; his number is 503-451-9872, and the post doesn't state a price, so ask when you call. Tillamook County Live has Hedler's offer featured at the top of the site through the flood window. No sign-up sheet, no waiting list, no agency involved — just two neighbors, a pile of sandbags, and a head start on the water.
stories.img_credit: Photo of a home ringed with sandbags against flood water by Jocelyn Augustino / FEMA via Wikimedia Commons, public domain (U.S. federal work; licensed photo, Tillamook County Live original, 2026-11-23).

stories.title: Thanksgiving Dinner Can Wait. The Tide Peaks at 1:02.
stories.summary: Most years, the biggest tides of the season arrive at inconvenient hours. This year the calendar is cooperating: the king tide window running Monday through Friday puts the highest water in the middle of the day, and on Thanksgiving Day the midday high tide at Netarts Bay is predicted for 1:02 p.m., at 8.30 feet. For scale, an ordinary afternoon high at Netarts two weeks ago was predicted at 6.09 feet, and Thursday's other high tide, at 2:18 in the morning, is only 6.00 feet. Wednesday's midday high is the week's biggest at 8.38 feet, and the top tide of the whole season lands at noon on Christmas Eve, 8.64 feet. If you go watch, the known spots are the pullouts along Netarts Bay Road, the fish hatchery, and the boat basin; at Oceanside, the parking area by the tunnel at Maxwell Point gives you the view without the beach. Cape Lookout's day-use area is closed for construction this winter, so use the trailhead instead. Watch from high ground and keep off the logs — this week's surf is running 30 to 40 feet on top of the tides. And if you take a good photo, the Oregon King Tides Project accepts submissions through its online form, so it can enter the state's long-term record.
stories.img_credit: Photo of a wave splashing in Good Fortune Cove at Cooks Chasm, just south of Cape Perpetua on the Oregon coast, by Joe Mabel via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 (licensed photo, Tillamook County Live original, 2026-11-23).

stories.title: Somebody in Pacific City Has a Holiday Dinner to Give Away
stories.summary: A full holiday dinner is looking for a family in Pacific City, and it started with one post in a Facebook group. On Friday afternoon, Sarah Christine posted in the What's Up Pacific City group that she is passing along a Samaritan Health Services holiday food coupon to someone in need. The coupon covers a frozen turkey up to 20 pounds, or a ham, plus a vegetable or fruit tray, lasagna, pies, or mixed nuts — in other words, the makings of a holiday table. She didn't have to post it. A coupon like that gets used quietly, or not at all; instead it went up in front of the whole group, offered to whoever needs it. Thanksgiving is Thursday, and somewhere in Pacific City there is a household doing the math on a holiday meal. If your household could use it, the post is in What's Up Pacific City under Sarah Christine's name — and if you have something similar sitting in a kitchen drawer this week, you know what to do with it.

stories.title: Meet Jumpin' Jack Flash, United Paws' Cat of the Week
stories.summary: United Paws' Cat of the Week is Jumpin' Jack Flash — a white-and-gray tabby with soft green eyes who was abandoned about two years ago and rescued anemic, malnourished and bone tired. With his fosters' help he is now healthy and happy: a talkative 'lover' and 'old soul,' in his foster's words, who grooms the other cats in the house and would like nothing more than a warm bed, a full tummy and a lap of his own. Meet-and-greets through unitedpaws.org.

stories.title: King tides meet a Super El Niño: 30-to-40-foot waves, a coastal flood warning, and a sneaker wave at Oceanside that went viral
stories.summary: The season's first king tides run Nov. 23–27, supercharged by a record-strong Super El Niño and slow-moving Kelvin waves that are already pushing 30-to-40-plus-foot surf onto the Oregon coast. A coastal flood warning runs Tuesday through Friday morning, with up to two feet of water possible above ground in low spots — and a TikTok video of a sneaker wave knocking a woman off her feet on the Oceanside Beach staircase has gone viral as the warning made waves. Locally, Netarts Bay's highest tide of the window hits at 1:02 p.m. on Thanksgiving Day (8.30 feet), and the season's top tide comes at noon on Christmas Eve.
stories.img_credit: Photo of king tides and big waves at Shore Acres on the Oregon coast by Bonnie Moreland via Wikimedia Commons, public domain (licensed photo, News Scout batch 2, 2026-11-23).

stories.title: Tillamook YMCA to offer after-hours access for shift workers

stories.title: The Big Tree of Rockaway Beach: a 1,000-year-old cedar that survived the 1700 Cascadia quake and tsunami, hiding in plain sight
stories.summary: At the end of a one-mile ADA-accessible boardwalk through the Cedar Wetlands Nature Preserve in Rockaway Beach stands one of the largest Western Red Cedars in North America — an estimated 800 to 1,200 years old, 154 feet tall, with a 49-foot trunk circumference. The tree survived coastal storms, fires, earthquakes and the 1700 Cascadia tsunami, in a nearly 50-acre old-growth cedar wetland tucked inside a residential neighborhood.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Jordan Wolfe / Oregon Coast TODAY (the story's own photo).
